title: Existence of an ample invertible module descends along finite locally free surjections
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a surjective finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. If $Y$ admits an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then $X$ admits an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, with ampleness in the absolute sense. No normality, Noetherianity, properness, finite-type hypothesis over a field, or descent datum for the supplied module is assumed.

proof.text: Choose an ample invertible module $M$ on $Y$. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $Y$ is quasi-compact. Pull an open cover of $X$ back to $Y$ and choose a finite subcover there; surjectivity of $f$ implies that the corresponding finitely many opens cover $X$. Hence $X$ is quasi-compact. Finiteness of $f$ is part of [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant], write $X=\coprod_{d\geq0}X_d$ as open and closed subschemes with $f_d:f^{-1}X_d	o X_d$ finite locally free of degree $d$. Surjectivity implies $X_0=\varnothing$: a degree-zero fibre has zero coordinate algebra and hence empty spectrum, whereas every fibre here has a point. For each $d\geq1$ choose the family $
u^{(d)}$ supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-function-norm] for $f_d$. Given $V\subseteq X$ open and $b\in\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$, define $
u_V(b)$ to be the unique regular function whose restriction to $V\cap X_d$ is $
u^{(d)}_{V\cap X_d}(b|_{f^{-1}(V\cap X_d)})$. Existence and uniqueness are exactly the structure-sheaf gluing axiom on the disjoint open cover [def-pc-scheme]; overlaps are empty. Multiplicativity, preservation of $1$ and restriction compatibility can each be checked on that cover and follow from the corresponding property of $
u^{(d)}$. If $b(y)=0$, the point $f(y)$ lies in a positive-degree piece and the vanishing property there gives $
u_V(b)(f(y))=0$. Thus one such family exists for $f$ without a constant-degree assumption. For empty $X$ use the unique function on every empty open.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (divisors-lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm) on the degree pieces of Morphisms Tag 04MH (morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free); the disjoint-cover assembly supplies the varying-degree case of 0BD4(1).

proof.text: Use the family $\nu_V$ constructed in step 2. By [lem-sfb-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs] choose an open cover $(V_i)$ of $X$ and generating sections $e_i$ of $M|_{f^{-1}V_i}$. Apply [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing] to these data and fix the resulting invertible module $N$ and frames $q_i$ on $X$. For every $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ this supplies a section $t\in\Gamma(X,N^{\otimes n})$, locally given by $t=\nu_{V_i}(b_i)q_i^{\otimes n}$ when $s=b_i e_i^{\otimes n}$. The module $N$ is fixed before choosing $s$ or $n$.

source.place: Tags 0BD2, 0BCY (divisors-lemma-norm-invertible) and 0BCZ (divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible); the norm line in 0BD0.

proof.text: For $x\in V_i$, frames identify nonvanishing of $s$ at points over $x$ with nonvanishing of $b_i$, and nonvanishing of $t$ at $x$ with nonvanishing of $\nu_{V_i}(b_i)$. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-function-norm-nonvanishing] hold: $f$ is finite, and steps 2 and 3 supply a multiplicative unital restriction-compatible family with the residue-field vanishing property. Its equivalence therefore gives $$X_t=\{x\in X:f^{-1}(\{x\})\subseteq Y_s\}.$$ This does not require a single integer degree or a scalar-power identity.

source.place: Tag 0BCZ, the zero-locus assertion, and Section 0BCX; applied to the local frame coefficients.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq X$, which exists by [def-pc-scheme]. The fibre $E=f^{-1}(\{x\})$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] to $Y,M,E$ and the open $f^{-1}V$. It gives $n>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ with $E\subseteq Y_s\subseteq f^{-1}V$. Take its norm section $t$ from step 3. The identity in step 4 implies $x\in X_t$. If $z\in X_t$, surjectivity gives $y\in f^{-1}(\{z\})$; then $y\in Y_s\subseteq f^{-1}V$, hence $z\in V$. Thus $x\in X_t\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 0BD0, choice of the finite fibre and Properties Tag 09NV (properties-lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] to the invertible module $N$, its positive tensor power $n$, its global section $t$, and the affine open $V$. It gives $V\cap X_t$ affine. Since $X_t\subseteq V$, this is $X_t$ itself. For every $x\in X$ we have therefore produced a positive-power global section of the single module $N$ with affine nonvanishing open containing $x$. Together with quasi-compactness from step 1 these are exactly the conditions of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], so $N$ is ample. If $X$ is empty the pointwise condition is vacuous and the same construction applies.
